title: Relative clauses
subtitle: who, which, where, whose, that, defining and non-defining

blocks.text: We use relative pronouns in relative clauses. We use relative clauses to give more information about something, without having to start a new sentence.

rows.example: What's the name of the man **who** created the Internet?
The experiment **which** worked was the last one.
This is the town **where** Albert Einstein was born.
That's the man **whose** sister discovered a new planet.

blocks.text: We can use **who** for animals when we give them a personality.

blocks.correct: Our dog, **who's** called Benji, is eight years old.
blocks.incorrect: Our dog, **which's** called Benji, is eight years old.

blocks.text: When there is a relative pronoun, remember not to repeat the subject/object.

blocks.correct: What's the name of the man **who** created the World Wide Web?
blocks.incorrect: What's the name of the man **who he** created the World Wide Web?

blocks.correct: This is the experiment **which** I'm doing at the moment.
blocks.incorrect: This is the experiment **which** I'm doing **it** at the moment.

blocks.text: Non-defining relative clauses give extra information. The sentence makes sense without the relative clause. If we remove the relative clause, the sentence still makes sense: That man over there started Microsoft.

rows.example: This program, **which** is totally free, protects your computer against viruses.

blocks.intro: We use commas with non-defining relative clauses.
items: Carl, **whose** sister is famous, is a friend of mine.

blocks.text: Defining relative clauses give very important information. If we remove a defining relative clause, the sentence doesn't make sense. Imagine that there are lots of people in a room. Only one of them is wearing a blue shirt. The person **who** is wearing the blue shirt started Microsoft. If we remove the relative clause, we won't know which person it is.

blocks.correct: The person **who** is wearing the blue shirt started Microsoft.
blocks.incorrect: The person started Microsoft. (We don't know which person.)

rows.use: To define who or what we are talking about
rows.example: This is the TV **which** works. This is the TV **which** doesn't work.

blocks.intro: We don't use commas with defining relative clauses. We can use **that** instead of **who** and **which**.
items: Did you see the programme about the woman **who** invented Tippex?
Did you see the programme about the woman **that** invented Tippex?

exercises.title: A · Relative pronouns
exercises.instruction: Complete using a word from the box. You may need some words more than once.

items.prompt: There's a film on tonight ___ I really want to see.
acceptedAnswers: which
that

items.prompt: Do you know any restaurants ___ they serve vegetarian dishes?
acceptedAnswers: where

items.prompt: Can you remember ___ told you about the new nightclub?
acceptedAnswers: who

items.prompt: The film, ___ stars Tom Hanks, is based on a book by Dan Brown.
acceptedAnswers: which

items.prompt: I've never met anyone before ___ mother was famous!
acceptedAnswers: whose

items.prompt: Lorenzo, ___ is from Spain originally, has lived here for about ten years.
acceptedAnswers: who

items.prompt: Carla, ___ parents are from Mexico, was born in the UK.
acceptedAnswers: whose

items.prompt: Here's a photo of the hotel ___ we stayed.
acceptedAnswers: where

exercises.title: B · Extra word
exercises.instruction: Write the extra word in each sentence.

items.prompt: The boy **who he** sits next to me in class is called Vladimir.
acceptedAnswers: he

items.prompt: This book, which I started reading **it** last week, is really funny.
acceptedAnswers: it

items.prompt: Jean, whose **her** mother is a nurse, wants to be a doctor.
acceptedAnswers: her

items.prompt: My mum and dad, who **they** got married fifteen years ago, met over thirty years ago.
acceptedAnswers: they

items.prompt: The jeans which I was telling you about **them** are over there.
acceptedAnswers: them

exercises.title: C · Join the sentences
exercises.instruction: Rewrite as one sentence using a relative clause.

items.prompt: My grandfather was an airline pilot. He is sixty-five years old now.
acceptedAnswers: My grandfather, who is sixty-five years old now, was an airline pilot.
My grandfather, who is sixty-five years old now, was an airline pilot

items.prompt: Friendly People is a comedy. It's my favourite programme.
acceptedAnswers: Friendly People, which is a comedy, is my favourite programme.
Friendly People, which is a comedy, is my favourite programme
Friendly People is a comedy which is my favourite programme.
Friendly People is a comedy which is my favourite programme

items.prompt: My friend Michael often comes to play with me. He hasn't got any brothers and sisters.
acceptedAnswers: My friend Michael, who hasn't got any brothers and sisters, often comes to play with me.
My friend Michael, who hasn't got any brothers and sisters, often comes to play with me

items.prompt: My sister loves wearing hats. Her hair is brown.
acceptedAnswers: My sister, whose hair is brown, loves wearing hats.
My sister, whose hair is brown, loves wearing hats

items.prompt: New York is an enormous city. It's where I was born.
acceptedAnswers: New York, where I was born, is an enormous city.
New York, where I was born, is an enormous city
New York is an enormous city where I was born.
New York is an enormous city where I was born

items.prompt: This CD is scratched. I only bought it yesterday.
acceptedAnswers: This CD, which I only bought yesterday, is scratched.
This CD, which I only bought yesterday, is scratched

items.prompt: My brother George has got some great shirts! He hates me borrowing his clothes.
acceptedAnswers: My brother George, who hates me borrowing his clothes, has got some great shirts!
My brother George, who hates me borrowing his clothes, has got some great shirts

items.prompt: Our neighbours have never invited us to dinner. Their house is directly opposite ours.
acceptedAnswers: Our neighbours, whose house is directly opposite ours, have never invited us to dinner.
Our neighbours, whose house is directly opposite ours, have never invited us to dinner

exercises.title: D · Picture prompts
exercises.instruction: Use the prompts to write sentences with a relative clause.

items.prompt: The tree / which / be / tall / not / have / any leaves
acceptedAnswers: The tree which is tall doesn't have any leaves.
The tree which is tall doesn't have any leaves
The tree which is tall does not have any leaves.
The tree that is tall doesn't have any leaves.

items.prompt: The trees / which / have / leaves / be / short
acceptedAnswers: The trees which have leaves are short.
The trees which have leaves are short
The trees that have leaves are short.
The trees that have leaves are short

items.prompt: The bottle / which / be / big / be / full
acceptedAnswers: The bottle which is big is full.
The bottle which is big is full
The bottle that is big is full.
The bottle that is big is full

items.prompt: The bottles / which / be / small / be / empty
acceptedAnswers: The bottles which are small are empty.
The bottles which are small are empty
The bottles that are small are empty.
The bottles that are small are empty

items.prompt: The girl / who / have / short hair / be called / Melissa
acceptedAnswers: The girl who has short hair is called Melissa.
The girl who has short hair is called Melissa
The girl that has short hair is called Melissa.
The girl that has short hair is called Melissa

items.prompt: The girls / whose / hair / be / long / be called / Lucy, Tina and Debbi
acceptedAnswers: The girls whose hair is long are called Lucy, Tina and Debbi.
The girls whose hair is long are called Lucy, Tina and Debbi

items.prompt: The boy / who / hold / a black basketball / wear / a school uniform
acceptedAnswers: The boy who is holding a black basketball is wearing a school uniform.
The boy who is holding a black basketball is wearing a school uniform
The boy who holds a black basketball wears a school uniform.
The boy that is holding a black basketball is wearing a school uniform.

items.prompt: The boys / who / have / basketballs / which / be / white / wear / tracksuits
acceptedAnswers: The boys who have basketballs which are white are wearing tracksuits.
The boys who have basketballs which are white are wearing tracksuits
The boys who have white basketballs are wearing tracksuits.
The boys who have white basketballs are wearing tracksuits

exercises.title: E · that or not?
exercises.instruction: Can the relative pronoun be replaced by that?

items.prompt: The tree which is tall doesn't have any leaves. (defining)
acceptedAnswers: that is possible

items.prompt: The trees which have leaves are short. (defining)
acceptedAnswers: that is possible

items.prompt: The bottle which is big is full. (defining)
acceptedAnswers: that is possible

items.prompt: The girls whose hair is long are called Lucy, Tina and Debbi. (whose)
acceptedAnswers: that is not possible

items.prompt: The boy who is holding a black basketball is wearing a school uniform. (defining who)
acceptedAnswers: that is possible

items.prompt: My grandfather, who is sixty-five years old now, was an airline pilot. (non-defining)
acceptedAnswers: that is not possible

that

acceptedAnswers: whose

items.prompt: It's a job ___ sounds quite interesting.
acceptedAnswers: which
that

items.prompt: Actuaries usually work for companies, like insurance companies, ___ deal with the chances of things happening in the future.
acceptedAnswers: which
that

items.prompt: For example, it's more probable that buildings will be flooded in places ___ it rains a lot.
acceptedAnswers: where

items.prompt: Greg's mum, ___ has been an actuary for about five years, is involved with car insurance.
acceptedAnswers: who

items.prompt: She works in an office ___ they decide how much car insurance people should pay.
acceptedAnswers: where

that
